summary: Intro/discovery call for Private VPC deployment. Horizon AI is evaluating Redwood Private vs Dedicated/Hosted. Main concerns: network topology, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints, egress and data residency, KMS integration, and audit logs. Next steps: share network guide, security pack, schedule deeper network deep-dive and provide pilot/benchmark plan.
topics: VPC peering vs Private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink)
transcript:
00:00:02 - Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, joining with mateo our solutions engineer and dana from customer success. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 - Priya: Hey this is priya, cto at horizon, Daniel here as lead infra, evan security, maya ml platform.
00:00:21 - Mateo: Great, thanks. High level we know you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private — today we want to focus on private/vpc networking constraints and success criteria.
00:00:35 - Daniel: Yeah primarily network questions. We run multi-account AWS, heavy use of Transit Gateway and some VPC peering. We need to understand how Redwood would hook in, what private endpoints look like, and any egress implications.
00:00:50 - Lena: Perfect. Before we dive, quick context — what's driving the private choice? compliance, latency, cost, or data residency?
00:00:59 - Priya: It's mostly compliance and data residency. We have EU customers and some regulated clients who require isolated infrastructure. Also our security team wants customer-managed keys and visibility into audit logs.
00:01:10 - Evan: Also prefer no public internet egress for inference traffic; want private connectivity.
00:01:16 - Lena: Understood. Mateo, can you give a short overview of the Private deployment options and networking patterns?
00:01:22 - Mateo: Sure. Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC as two main patterns: 1) PrivateLink / interface endpoints — Redwood exposes an endpoint service and you create an interface endpoint in your account, traffic stays on AWS private network. 2) VPC Peering / Cross-account peering — route-based peering or via Transit Gateway where our Private control plane talks to your runtime or we host in a customer VPC. For bigger customers we often recommend Transit Gateway for scalability, peering works but has CIDR overlap constraints.
00:01:57 - Daniel: ok so with PrivateLink, it's an endpoint in our subnet, that handles API communication? What about the inference data plane — where does the GPU runtime live?
00:02:07 - Mateo: good question. There are two deployment models: 1) Redwood-managed runtime in a dedicated VPC we own — in that case you use PrivateLink or peering to reach the control/API plane and we route inference traffic over private connectivity to the runtime. 2) Customer-hosted runtime — we provide an appliance or Terraform and you run the runtime in your account on your GPUs; then everything is internal to your VPC and you have full control of egress.
00:02:30 - Priya: We were hoping to avoid managing GPUs ourselves. The idea would be a Redwood-hosted runtime but accessible only over private networking. Is that supported?
00:02:37 - Mateo: Yes, supported. We can set up a PrivateLink endpoint service and set up interface endpoints in your account. Alternatively, we can peer directly and create routes so traffic never hits the public internet. There are tradeoffs: PrivateLink provides cross-account private connectivity with AWS-managed interface endpoints and is easier for SSO/cert management, but it incurs NLB costs and needs ENIs in your subnet. Peering can be cheaper but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table management.
00:03:05 - Daniel: We use 10.0.0.0/8 ranges a lot; CIDR overlap is a real risk. Transit Gateway is our standard for cross-account. How does Redwood integrate with TGW?
00:03:16 - Mateo: We can peer to your TGW or attach to a shared VPC. For TGW — usually customers set up a VPC for Redwood endpoints and attach it to the TGW, or we attach our peering VPC to your TGW. We'll need the account IDs and attachment permissions. That model avoids CIDR overlap problems generally.
00:03:35 - Evan: What about IP whitelisting / security groups? Our security posture requires tight SGs and private subnets with no internet egress except through specified NAT.
00:03:44 - Lena: Totally reasonable. With PrivateLink you control which subnets host the ENIs and security groups. We recommend placing interface endpoints in private subnets with SG rules allowing only your app subnets. For peering, you control route tables and SGs on your side; we document recommended SG rules.
00:04:01 - Maya: For the inference data — do we send large payloads over the PrivateLink? We have use cases with multi-MB context windows. Concerned about throughput and cost.
00:04:12 - Mateo: Yes payloads go over the private link. Throughput is generally fine but depends on NLB sizing and ENI bandwidth; we can architect for large messages by ensuring adequate subnets and using ENIs across AZs. Cost side — data processing over PrivateLink has transfer charges; we'll include an estimate in the pricing. If very large data, consider co-locating runtime in your account to avoid cross-account transfer.
00:04:35 - Daniel: And region constraints — we have EU-West-1 and a smaller EU-West-3 presence. Does Redwood host in those regions for Private option?
00:04:44 - Lena: We have region coverage for Private in most major regions; I'll check exact availability for EU-West-3. For Dedicated we can provision in your preferred region; for Hosted we have multi-region but Private sometimes needs pre-provisioning. We'll confirm region availability in the follow-up.
00:04:58 - Priya: KMS — we need customer-controlled keys, ideally CMK in our account that Redwood can use to decrypt payloads or at-rest keys. Is that possible?
00:05:06 - Mateo: We support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. If you run the runtime in your account, you control the keys. For Redwood-hosted runtime with private connectivity, we offer options: bring-your-own-key via cross-account grants or use an envelope encryption model where we never see plaintext keys. This requires some setup and IAM roles. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
00:05:26 - Evan: Audit logs — we need detailed request/response audit logs and token-level cost attribution. Also retention policies and the ability to push logs to our S3 or CloudWatch.
00:05:36 - Lena: Redwood Console supports token-level cost/latency breakdowns and can stream logs to your CloudWatch or S3 via Kinesis Firehose for Private deployments. We'll include the log export patterns and retention options.
00:05:49 - Daniel: Any network ports we need to open? Mostly egress 443?
00:05:53 - Mateo: Typically 443 for API/control traffic. If you host GPUs in your account, internal ports for runtime-to-runtime (gRPC) are often required — we'll document the port list. For PrivateLink, interface endpoints use TLS over 443.
00:06:06 - Priya: What about failover — if an AZ goes down, how does connectivity behave?
00:06:11 - Mateo: We recommend creating interface endpoints across multiple AZs or attaching across TGW; runtime clusters are multi-AZ. We'll also recommend health checks and route failover. We'll propose an HA design in the deep-dive.
00:06:22 - Lena: Quick question on timeline and success criteria — what's your pilot look like?
00:06:27 - Priya: We're targeting a 6-week pilot to validate latency and quality on 2 models, about 50 rps peak, and integration with our app in EU-West-1. Success: sub-100ms p99 for short prompts, and cost under our threshold.
00:06:39 - Maya: Also need to validate SSO and audit pipelines.
00:06:42 - Lena: Ok good, we'll include those targets in the benchmark plan.
00:06:46 - Daniel: One more — ingress from our on-prem data center. We have Direct Connect into our TGW. Will that be supported?
00:06:53 - Mateo: Yes — if your TGW is the entry point you can reach Redwood endpoints via peering or PrivateLink through the TGW. We'll need to validate route propagation and ensure the Direct Connect routes are present.
00:07:05 - Evan: On the compliance front, can you share your SOC2 report and specifics about encryption in transit?
00:07:10 - Lena: We'll share the SOC2 pack and redacted reports via the secure links. Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+ for API and optional mTLS for customer-hosted runtimes.
00:07:20 - Priya: Any special considerations for multi-region data residency? We store EU data in EU and would like inference data to stay in EU too.
00:07:28 - Mateo: We'll ensure runtime and model weights for EU customers are provisioned in EU regions for the pilot. If you need strict data residency we recommend Dedicated or Customer-hosted runtime in your region.
00:07:38 - Lena: Let's talk cost tradeoffs quickly — PrivateLink + Redwood-hosted runtime has managed convenience but can have incremental per-GB transfer and NLB charges; Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable unit costs but requires commitments; customer-hosted eliminates cross-account transfer but requires infra ops.
00:07:55 - Priya: Our procurement team will want numbers. We'll need an apples-to-apples cost estimate including expected transfer.
00:08:02 - Lena: We'll include that in the follow-up pricing sheet. Mateo will include bandwidth and ENI assumptions.
00:08:09 - Maya: Integration-wise, how do we authenticate? API keys or SAML? We want SSO for developer access and RBAC.
00:08:17 - Mateo: For control plane UI and console access we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For API, we can do short-lived tokens and we support mTLS for private connections. RBAC maps to org roles in the console and can be synced via SCIM.
00:08:32 - Daniel: Any PII considerations in logs? We need redaction options and the ability to not store raw responses.
00:08:38 - Lena: We support configurable retention and can redact or avoid storing raw responses in the logs. For regulated workloads we recommend customer-hosted runtime.
00:08:48 - Evan: How about egress billing if runtime is in our VPC vs yours?
00:08:53 - Mateo: If runtime is in your VPC, no cross-account data transfer charges from AWS between runtime and your app. If runtime in Redwood-hosted VPC and you call via PrivateLink, you pay PrivateLink data charges and there may be cross-AZ transfer costs — we'll quantify.
00:09:10 - Priya: Ok, that's the bulk. Any blockers on timeline from your side?
00:09:14 - Lena: No blockers, we just need the CIDRs and a couple account IDs to set up a test endpoint. We'll also schedule the SE network deep-dive with your infra team.
00:09:23 - Daniel: We'll send CIDRs and TGW details after the call.
00:09:27 - Mateo: Great. One follow-up - for the pilot, which models should we test?
00:09:31 - Maya: Our initial test set: 1) a small LLM for chat summarization 2) a larger 8B classification model. We'll share prompts and throughput targets.
00:09:41 - Lena: Perfect. We'll create a tailored benchmark plan.
00:09:44 - Priya: Thanks, this was helpful.
00:09:47 - Lena: we'll recap next steps.
00:09:49 - Dana: Quick note, i'll open a slack channel and send the deck and the security pack after the call.
00:09:55 - Daniel: thanks.
00:10:00 - Lena: Alright team, we'll follow up with network checklist, security docs, pricing, and schedule the deep-dive. Any final questions?
00:10:09 - Priya: None from me.
00:10:11 - Evan: all good.
00:10:13 - Lena: Great—thanks everyone.
00:10:20 - [END OF CALL - NOTE: actual call continued with brief offline questions and screen-share of a sample Terraform VPC configuration; transcript clipped by recorder]
